prompt: The given bar chart how many residents in UK spend their money in three categories (Food and drinks, Resturants and hotels, Entertainment) during 2004.
essay:
The bar chart illustrates the percentage of expenditure allocated to three categories—food and drink, restaurants and hotels, and entertainment—across five age brackets in the UK during the year 2004.  Overall, expenditure on food and drink increased steadily with age. Conversely, younger citizens directed a larger share of their budgets to restaurants and hotels, while entertainment spending peaked among middle-aged to senior residents (61–75 years).

For food and drink, residents aged under 30 spent the lowest proportion, accounting for roughly 6% of their budget. This figure rose consistently across older demographics, climbing to 13% for 31–45 year-olds and reaching a peak of approximately 23% among those aged 61 and above.  In contrast, spending on restaurants and hotels followed a generally reverse trend. The under-30 demographic spent the highest proportion on this category at 14%. This proportion declined across older groups, dropping to a low of just 2% among individuals aged 61 to 75, before rising slightly to around 7% for those 76 and older.  Regarding entertainment, spending remained relatively modest for people under 45, hovering at around 7%. However, it rose sharply for the 46–60 age bracket (14%) and peaked at 23% among 61–75 year-olds, before dropping back to 13% for those over 76.
